{"id":"042225e0-1f7e-4b01-82df-fe6b7e35af7a","object":"chat.completion","created":1790500406,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"requirements":[{"requirement_id":"R1","status":"unsupported","supported_by":[]},{"requirement_id":"R2","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C1"]},{"requirement_id":"R3","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C1"]},{"requirement_id":"R4","status":"unsupported","supported_by":[]},{"requirement_id":"R5","status":"unsupported","supported_by":[]},{"requirement_id":"R6","status":"unsupported","supported_by":[]}]}","reasoning_content":"We need answer JSON only. Need evaluate each requirement status based on claims. We have one claim C1: Sophie died accidental fall in Athens, Greece. Original skeleton requirements:
R1 Charity and first-name relation: musical artist shares first name with part of charity's name; charity unrelated; registered 2000-2010 inclusive. Claim only says Sophie Scottish DJ producer died. Does it establish shares first name with part of charity? No. Unsupported.
R2 Death city and aviation-site relation: artist died in a city 20-30 miles from site of country's deadliest aviation accident as of 2023. Claim says died in Athens, Greece (city). Does not mention aviation accident site/distance. No support? It establishes death city Athens. Requirement includes relation to aviation accident site. That is material part? It establishes death city, but not 20-30 miles relation. Is that partially_supported? The requirement: "This musical artist died in a city that is 20 to 30 miles (inclusive) away from the site of that country’s deadliest aviation accident (as of 2023)." It has material parts: artist died in a city; city is 20-30 miles from site; site is country's deadliest aviation accident as of 2023. Claim establishes death in Athens. Does that count as substantive material part? Yes, the artist died in a city (Athens). But the core relation remains unsupported. Partially supported? Need decide. The claim: Sophie died in Athens, Greece. That establishes "This musical artist died in a city..." but the requirement is specifically city 20-30 miles away from site. It establishes that artist died in a city, but not the relation. Is "died in a city" a substantive material part? I think yes. The requirement includes relation; death city identification maybe supports entity. But requirement is about relation between death city and aviation site. Does establishing death city alone count? It is a material part, because to establish relation you need death city. However maybe requirement is a compound: artist died in a city that is 20-30 miles away from site. Claim gives death city. But no distance. So partially_supported.

R3 Accident-to-death interval: aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to artist's accidental death. Claim says Sophie died accidental on 30 Jan 2021. Does not mention aviation accident/date. Unsupported? It establishes accidental death date but not accident occurred 15 years prior. Requirement: "The aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to the artist’s accidental death." Material parts: there was an aviation accident; it occurred 15 years before death; artist's death was accidental. Claim establishes artist's death was accidental and date. Does that support a substantive part? It supports the artist's accidental death (date). But the main relation is interval. Is that partial? Hmm. The requirement is specifically about aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to artist's accidental death. Claim doesn't mention aviation accident. It supports the artist's accidental death. Could be partial? Need apply definitions: partially_supported: Verified Claims establish at least one substantive material part of requirement, but one or more material parts remain unsupported. If requirement includes artist's accidental death, yes. But is that a material part of "The aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to the artist’s accidental death"? The phrase includes artist's accidental death as referent. But requirement's core is interval. It might be considered partial because we know death was accidental, but not accident. However if the requirement is entirely about accident and interval, and the death being accidental is a precondition. I'd lean partially_supported? Need consistency.

R4 Partner interview and song-reference relation: partner at time of death gave interview saying after death, artist has become direct reference to one of their songs. Claim only death details. No partner, no interview, no song reference. Unsupported.
R5 Song-title form: title is one word, adjective. Claim no song. Unsupported.
R6 Requested song title: What is song title? Claim no song title. Unsupported.

But need careful: "For every Task Requirement assign exactly one status". We can cite C1 for partial if applicable. Need decide R2 and R3.

Let's examine claim C1: "Sophie (Sophie Xeon), a Scottish DJ and producer, died aged 34 on 30 January 2021 after an accidental fall while watching the full moon; the accident was reported to have taken place in Athens, Greece."

This establishes:
- There is a musical artist? Scottish DJ and producer likely musical artist. "Sophie" shares first name with part of charity? No.
- Died in Athens, Greece. City? Athens. It says accident took place in Athens, Greece. It might be city. So R2 partial: establishes artist died in a city (Athens), but not distance to aviation site or that country's deadliest accident.
- Died accidentally on 30 Jan 2021. R3 partial? It establishes artist's accidental death date. The aviation accident not mentioned. So partial? The requirement demands aviation accident occurred 15 years prior. The claim establishes accidental death date, but not relation. It is a substantive part? The date of death and accident nature. I'd say yes, partially supported because at least the artist's accidental death is established. But is "artist's accidental death" a material part of R3? R3's source span: "The aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to the artist’s accidental death." It contains two events: aviation accident and artist's accidental death, plus temporal relation. Claim establishes artist's accidental death. So partial.

What about R1: Does C1 establish "musical artist shares their first name with part of a charity’s name"? No. It establishes musical artist named Sophie. Does that support shares first name? No, no charity. Unsupported. It also doesn't establish charity registered 2000-2010. Unsupported.

R4: Claim establishes artist, death. Partner? No. Unsupported.
R5: No song. Unsupported.
R6: No song title. Unsupported.

Need output JSON exactly. supported_by for unsupported must be empty. For partial, cite C1. For R2 and R3 partially_supported with C1. For R1? Could "Sophie" name support part of requirement "musical artist shares first name..."? It establishes musical artist has first name Sophie, but not shares with charity. Is that a substantive material part? The requirement is relation: musical artist shares their first name with part of charity's name. Having a first name is trivial? It might be material? But no charity. Definition: Mere entity-name overlap, candidate mention, prior search direction, or background context does not count. The claim establishes identity/name of artist, but not relation to charity. I think unsupported. For R2 and R3, however, the claim establishes death city and accidental death, which are referents in requirement. Are those "mere entity-name overlap" or actual material parts? R2: "died in a city that is 20 to 30 miles away from the site..." The claim gives death city. That's a substantive part (the city). R3: "artist's accidental death" is established. That's a substantive part. So partial.

But wait, R2 might be considered fully unsupported because the requirement is specifically that the city is 20-30 miles from the site of deadliest aviation accident; merely knowing the city does not establish that relation. But the definition of partially_supported allows "at least one substantive material part". Is "artist died in a city" a material part? Yes, because the requirement requires that the artist died in a city (as opposed to elsewhere) and that city has a relation. The claim confirms death in Athens, a city. It doesn't confirm relation. So partial.

R3: "aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to the artist's accidental death." The claim confirms the artist's accidental death on 30 Jan 2021. That is a material part. Partial.

Need ensure not infer "Athens is a city" from outside? Claim says "taken place in Athens, Greece." Athens is commonly a city, but do we use outside knowledge? The claim states "Athens, Greece" but doesn't explicitly say city. However "Athens" is a city. But rules say do not use outside knowledge. Is "Athens is a city" outside knowledge? The claim says "taken place in Athens, Greece." It doesn't say city. But the requirement uses "died in a city". The claim says accident took place in Athens. We might need outside knowledge to know Athens is a city. But "Athens" is likely recognized as a city. However rule 4: Do not use outside knowledge. We can only use claim text. Claim doesn't explicitly label Athens as a city. But "Athens, Greece" in natural language implies a city? Maybe not. It could be a place. But for this task, should we treat "Athens" as city? The claim says "in Athens, Greece", and the original question says died in a city. The claim says accident took place in Athens. Athens is a city. But if we cannot use outside knowledge, we might not know. However the claim itself: "the accident was reported to have taken place in Athens, Greece." It doesn't state Athens is a city. But the requirement's material part "died in a city" might not be directly stated. But it's common knowledge. The rules say no outside knowledge. So strictly, C1 does not establish "Athens is a city". It says "Athens, Greece" but not "city". Should we consider this unsupported? Hmm. The claim states "died aged 34 ... accident ... taken place in Athens, Greece." It implies place. The requirement says died in a city. Without outside knowledge, we can't confirm Athens is a city. But maybe the phrase "Athens, Greece" is a location, and Athens is a city; this is common geographic knowledge. The instruction "Do not use outside knowledge" might mean don't know factual relationships not in claims. But interpreting "Athens" as a city might be considered outside knowledge. However in many similar tasks, we can use common sense? The instructions are strict. But the claim explicitly says "Athens, Greece" - the name Athens is widely known as a city. But to be safe, maybe R2 should be unsupported because it doesn't establish the distance relation, and the city part is not explicitly established as city. But partially_supported requires at least one substantive material part. The claim establishes death in Athens, which is the city in question if Athens is a city. The requirement: "died in a city that is 20 to 30 miles ... away from the site..." The claim establishes "died in Athens." If Athens is a city, then it establishes the death city. But it doesn't establish the distance. So partial.

What about R3: claim establishes "artist's accidental death" on date. It says "died aged 34 ... after an accidental fall". So accidental death is established. That's material. Partial.

Should R2 be partially_supported? I think yes.

Let's check if any claim supports R4? No.

R6 "What is the song title?" This is the question. It asks for answer. The requirement is to provide song title. No claim gives song title. Unsupported. It might be considered fully unsupported.

Need output JSON. Use exact requirement IDs. supported_by arrays. For unsupported, empty arrays? The format shows supported_by for fully supported. For unsupported, rule 10: supported_by must be empty. So [].
For partially, supported_by: ["C1"].
For R1: []
R2: ["C1"]
R3: ["C1"]
R4: []
R5: []
R6: []

But wait: R1 might be partially supported because C1 establishes a musical artist named Sophie. Requirement: "A musical artist shares their first name with part of a charity’s name. The charity is unrelated to the musical artist, and was registered between 2000 and 2010 (inclusive)." Does C1 establish "A musical artist"? Yes, Sophie is Scottish DJ and producer, a musical artist. But the requirement is "A musical artist shares their first name with part of a charity’s name." The existence of a musical artist is a material part? The requirement is relational: musical artist shares first name with part of charity name. The claim establishes a musical artist exists (Sophie). But it does not establish the relation. Is that a substantive material part? It might be, because the requirement presupposes a musical artist. However the definition says "partially_supported: establish at least one substantive material part of the requirement". The existence of the musical artist is a material part. But then almost every requirement involving a musical artist would be partially supported by C1. Is that intended? The rules say "Mere entity-name overlap, entity mention, candidate mention, prior search direction, or background context does not count as support." C1 mentions a musical artist, which is the subject. But does it establish the requirement? The requirement is specifically about the sharing relation. Establishing that there is a musical artist is not enough to establish the sharing relation. But it is a material part? I'd lean that it's not a substantive part of the specific requirement "shares their first name with part of charity's name" because the core is the sharing. The existence of the artist is background. However for R2, the core is distance relation, but the claim establishes death city. Is that different? The death city is one of the two endpoints of the relation. For R1, the artist's first name is one endpoint. C1 gives the first name Sophie. But no charity. So it establishes the artist's first name. Is that a material part? The requirement is "shares their first name with part of charity's name." It requires the artist has a first name, and charity has part of its name matching. C1 gives artist's first name. Could be partial. But then R1 would be partially supported. Need decide.

Similarly R4: requirement "partner of artist gave interview..." C1 establishes artist and death. But not partner. Could be partial? It establishes the artist (whose partner). But that's background. The core is partner interview and song reference. I'd say unsupported.

The instructions emphasize: "A Task Requirement is NOT evidence. Its presence in the Task Skeleton does not mean that it is true, that its referent exists, or that it has already been established." "Mere topical relevance, entity-name overlap, candidate mention, prior search direction, or background context does not count as support." So just establishing the artist exists is background context, not support for the specific requirement. For R2, the requirement is about the death city and its relation to aviation accident site. The claim establishes death city. Is that background? It is one of the specific facts: "This musical artist died in a city that is..." The claim establishes the artist died in Athens. That is a specific material part: the death location. It's not just the artist exists; it's the death city. So that should count. For R3, claim establishes accidental death date. That is a specific material part of "aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to artist's accidental death." The artist's accidental death is a specific fact. So partial.

For R1, the claim establishes the artist's first name is Sophie? It says "Sophie (Sophie Xeon)". So first name Sophie. Requirement: shares first name with part of charity's name. The first name is one endpoint. But the sharing relation is the core. Does establishing the first name count as a substantive material part? It is a specific fact: the artist's first name. But the requirement is about the sharing. I'd argue it's a material part because to compare, you need the first name. But there is no charity. However the requirement has two parts: (a) musical artist shares first name with part of charity's name; (b) charity unrelated and registered 2000-2010. Claim establishes musical artist's first name Sophie. That's a material part of (a)? Maybe. But the sharing is not established. So could be partially_supported. Let's think of grading: If a requirement is "X shares first name with part of charity Y", and evidence says "X's first name is Sophie", does that partially support? It establishes the first name of X, which is a necessary component. But the requirement is not "X has a first name"; it's "X shares first name with part of charity". The existence of a first name is presupposed. The material condition is the sharing. So I'd say unsupported. The claim doesn't establish any part of the sharing relation. It just identifies the artist. That's background. The rule about entity-name overlap not counting suggests that just names don't count. So R1 unsupported.

For R2, the material conditions: artist died in a city; the city is 20-30 miles from site of country's deadliest aviation accident as of 2023. Claim establishes artist died in Athens (if city). That's one material condition (death city). It doesn't establish distance or accident. So partial.

For R3: material conditions: aviation accident occurred; 15 years prior to artist's accidental death. Claim establishes artist's accidental death date. That's one material condition (the death was accidental and date). So partial.

For R4: material conditions: partner at time of death; gave an interview; said following death, artist has become direct reference to one of their songs. Claim establishes artist died. No partner or interview. Unsupported.

For R5: title is one word, adjective. No song. Unsupported.

For R6: song title. No song title. Unsupported.

Thus final.
